name: 4-20 mA Signal Scaling
description: Converts a linear 4-20mA transmitter signal to an engineering value given the lower and upper range values.
variables: PV = process value, I = current signal (mA), LRV/URV = lower/upper range values
application: Any linear 4-20mA transmitter or I/O card scaling
assumptions: Linear transmitter response, no damping/offset error

name: Orifice Plate Flow
description: Volumetric flow rate through a square-edged concentric orifice plate.
variables: Q = flow, Cd = discharge coefficient, E = velocity of approach factor, d = bore, ΔP = differential pressure, ρ = density, β = d/D
assumptions: Fully developed turbulent flow, square-edged plate, incompressible fluid

name: Liquid Valve Sizing (Cv)
description: Required flow coefficient for a control valve in non-flashing, non-cavitating liquid service.
variables: Cv = valve flow coefficient, Q = flow rate, ΔP = pressure drop, SG = specific gravity
assumptions: No flashing/cavitation, negligible piping geometry factor (Fp≈1)

name: Plant Heat Rate
description: Relates thermal efficiency to the fuel energy required per unit of electrical output.
application: Thermal power plant performance and fuel cost estimation

name: RTD Callendar-Van Dusen
description: Standard resistance-temperature relationship for platinum RTDs.
assumptions: IEC 60751 class curve, negligible self-heating and lead-wire error

name: DP-Flow Square Root Relationship
description: Differential-pressure flow transmitters produce a signal proportional to the square of flow; extraction linearizes it.
variables: Flow% = percent of max flow, ΔP% = percent of max differential pressure
example: ΔP at 25% of span → Flow = √0.25 = 50% of max flow
assumptions: Beta ratio and fluid density constant across the range

name: Hydrostatic Pressure / Level
description: Pressure exerted by a column of liquid, used for level measurement via pressure/DP transmitters.
variables: P = pressure, ρ = fluid density, g = gravitational acceleration, h = liquid column height

name: PID Controller (parallel form)
formula: Output = Bias + Kp·e + Ki·∫e dt + Kd·de/dt
variables: e = SP−PV error, Kp/Ki/Kd = gains, Bias = output at zero error
application: Process control loop tuning and output prediction
assumptions: Linear control law, no output clamping/anti-windup modeled

name: Reynolds Number (pipe flow)
description: Dimensionless number indicating laminar vs turbulent flow regime.
variables: ṁ = mass flow rate, μ = dynamic viscosity, D = pipe internal diameter
application: Flow meter selection, discharge coefficient validity checks

name: Pump Head & Hydraulic Power
description: Shaft power required to deliver a given flow against a given head at a stated pump efficiency.
variables: ρ = density, Q = flow (m3/s), H = head (m), η = pump efficiency (fraction)
assumptions: Constant density, steady flow, efficiency includes hydraulic+mechanical losses
